bestBets.overview: If the BOM is any guide this track will remain soft, all gets down to when and how much is in the showers forecast for Wednesday. What we do know is the rail is out a whopping 11m. Kick things off with a 1350m Maiden Plate. Looks a 'no pace race' on paper. Dare say no's 1,2 & 8 will be settling forward. INDAMOUSE appeals. Back to back 4ths but better efforts than they read. Draws much better here, doubt this time will be restrained to settle so far back. KONIGSTEIN is new blood, sent north by Waller after just one run in NSW. EMPHATIC hasn't had much luck this time in, placed 1st-up and 2nd-up then was slow out and encountered traffic when unplaced latest. This could be the one getting all favours in transit. HARU didn't appear fancied on debut, things went awry at the start, give thought. WELCOME ADVICE resuming new blood now with Jack Bruce. Trialed 2nd then 1st, the one it beat last start went to Ballina, sp'd odds-on and won by a space.

raceTips.comment: Doomben racing on Wednesday with an 11m rail. As of 7.30am this morning the weather forecast is for 2 to 15mm however looking at the radar there's not much, if anything about. Current rating a Good (4). Interesting 1350m maiden to get the day underway, Chris Waller with a couple of interesting runners being Konigstein who closed from last on debut at Kembla & first starter Sir Arrogonce who has trialled ok, both definite market watches. Indamouse looks close, probably doesn't want the track too wet though & that looks likely to play in his favour.

raceTips.comment: I'm with the Kelly Schweida trained duo Metric & Summer Sensation here however which one as both appear ready to break through. Light leaning to the latter with the likelihood of a dry track, her stablemate gives me the impression she may be better suited on rain affected ground. Game in defeat at the Sunshine Coast sitting wide throughout, would have won with a more economical trip. Tony Gollan's Easy Feeling has trialled well & I'd be surprised if not in the finish.

bestBets.overview: 1200m 3yo Maiden Plate for the blokes. As things stand (with a few already out) there will be three on debut, two resuming, three 2nd-up having just their 2nd start, and two 2nd-up having just their 3rd start. Map says no's 2,3,9,11 can be contributing to the pace. Really liked what I saw of RED POINT on debut - bit slow out, keen, hampered, held-up - my video summary read like a stewards report on steroids! The Andrew Parramore trained WEOWNACHEVY was rock-solid when resuming. Tempo suit the winner, this son of Winning Rupert refused to wave a white flag. A claim for the 'rising star' Bella Youngberry, a shrewd  move. Market moves with the resuming CAPTAIN BLOOD and newcomer VUKA must be respected. Decent yards to put it mildly.

raceTips.comment: Open looking maiden over the 1200m. Morning line favourite Weownachevy stuck on well last start sitting up front on a slick tempo, form out of that race now proven in Saturday company (Exceed The Sale). The rise in trip looks suitable based on that. Red Point a market watch which is the norm from the stable. Debut effort was a good one making ground at the end of 1000m at Eagle Farm when solid in betting. Newcomer to the Gollan yard Captain Blood has been trialling well & should be ready to go, big threat.

First thoughts can only be set in chalk.  Map says no's 1,2,3,7,8,10,11,12,14,15,16,19 each boast pace. How many remain is essential to know if you'd rather do proper form and analysis and/or bet off someone who does just that. Right now I am bullish with CAPITAL CHORD, and keeping MAQUISA in mind.

raceTips.comment: Plenty of acceptors however a max of 12 to run post scratchings. A number of these come into the race off last start maiden wins. Dyami isn't one of those with his recent form being in Class 1 company so he rises nothing in grade. Gate 1, top jock on with his claim & positive wet track form he looks well placed. Cryptic Beauty resumes with some solid form lines last prep & will race on speed for Emily Lang. Tasman Bay may not have beaten a great deal at the Sunshine Coast however he did it in impressive fashion, definite claims to handle the class rise.

bestBets.overview: 1660m C5. Note only nine can run. As things stand Waller is good for three (circa 33% of the field) so unfortunately you've gotta drill down on what the market does with no's 4,5,6  before you can place a bet responsibly aka with 'utmost confidence'. Map's not at easy to rely upon in these circumstances BUT says emphatically 2 leads from 5 & 10, race run to suit all three. For now I am thinking you bank on GORBACHEV going back to back - the 2nd-up win was full of merit, after the claim a mere half kilo less  today. And the 'two from three' track stat hits one in the eye like the proverbial pizza pie. BARBRAY displayed a lovely turn of hoof latest, three 'on the bounce'  would come as no surprise. LOVEY DOVEY blew the start once again when resuming, did okay, but at the same time proved there is no trainer capable of remedying such things with some horses.

raceTips.comment: Lovey Dovey did me no favours whatsoever last prep however I'm either loyal or stupid tipping her here. She holds a good second up record, made ground after a bad start when resuming (1350m) & is sharp enough to run well at the mile trip on a surface with give in it which she prefers. The engagement of Ben Thompson is another positive. Rock Hard Love looks close, beaten an eyelash last start whilst Gorbachev must be included off the last start win.

bestBets.overview: 1200m C3. A dozen can partake. Four early scratchings could see Gollan with no fewer than four, perhaps five 'locking horns'. As things stand Heathcote is good for two, Kendrick is also good for two too, and M Dunn might wind up with two too. Hence once again one finds themselves swimming against the tide. Add to that five could be resuming. All the feels of a 'shipwreck coast'  that will pound you onto them rocks. Glass less than half-full. One is left with no option than to read them tea-leaves. The map says no's 5,8,10,11,18 will supply the pace.  Alas my selections are set in tissue. Right now FLAXLANDS looks a decent hope.  The resuming mare AMUSEMANTES on her deeds to date could well have the last laugh.

raceTips.comment: Max of 12 to go around once again. Dark Arts has trialled well & clearly looks the toughest to beat. Placed 2 of 5 fresh runs note only one of those has been with the Gollan yard which was of course the latest when narrowly going under at the Sunshine Coast. Amuseantes right in the mix also, trialled well enough to win fresh.

bestBets.overview: 1350m BM68. A dozen can run. The map has changed considerably. Had five runners going forward, now just the 2 remains.  Waller could have been good for six, has settled upon three.  Hoysted had two, now just the one. I am thinking RIMBAUD could be as good a chance as any. If they are swooping I'm all over HEADHUNTER. And then there's the luckless HURRICANE LU. Goodness me. Don't often see a horse run well so often and for one reason or another have no luck. My highlight, engaging a 3 kg claimer who due to his weight couldn't claim one ounce. Give it strength.

raceTips.comment: Lots of if's & but's surround this closing race, who will run & who won't plus the track condition. Hurricane Lu continues to race well without winning, her recent efforts in stronger races have been good ones & I like her coming back in trip. Flaxlands either didn't handle the rise in grade last start or the dry surface. Her record tells you she's a mare who races best with give in the ground, will she get that today though?
